papers.title: Massive failure of <scp>T</scp>i<scp>N</scp>b<scp>N</scp> coating in surface engineered metal‐on‐metal hip arthroplasty: Retrieval analysis
papers.abstract: This article presents examination of a failed total hip replacement with surface engineered metal-on-metal (MoM) articulation. The implant was coated with a thin TiNbN film (Physical Vapor Deposition), and at retrieval 53 months after implantation the coating was abraded on weight-bearing part of the head and acetabular component. Scanning electron microscopy of bearing surfaces demonstrated multifocal crack formation, delamination of small film fragments, and formation of aggregates containing nanometer sized wear debris. We also observed coating damage in third body mechanism. Complex failure mechanism of TiNbN coating demonstrated in this study suggests insufficient bonding strength between the coating and substrate alloy and raise concerns regarding the use of such coatings in total hip arthroplasty with MoM bearing. © 2015 Wiley Periodicals, Inc. J Biomed Mater Res Part B: Appl Biomater, 104B: 1043-1049, 2016.

papers.title: Problem-based approach in property law – a university’s strategy in focus
papers.abstract: This paper examines a teaching method in property law. It is a method that applies the use of tutorials to complement the traditional delivery of lectures. The tutorials are run using group teaching techniques, allowing the students to be engaged in active learning. Independent, individual and group research work is involved throughout the process. The paper explores the benefits and problems associated with the operation of this teaching method. Further, it examines the alignment of the problem-based learning strategy to the global vision of universities to push the boundaries of learning through teaching and research, enterprise and professional practice. The paper explains how using tutorials in this teaching method fits with the dimensions of the United Kingdom Professional Standards Framework (UKPSF) for teaching and supporting learning, and the underpinning objectives of the named university’s learning strategy.

papers.title: Evaluating Two Sparse Grid Surrogates for Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: One obstacle to conducting uncertainty quantification in groundwater modeling is the computational cost of solving partial differential equations that describe groundwater flow and solute transport. This is especially true for recently developed techniques such as Markov chain Monte Carlo and global sensitivity analysis. A recent trend is to develop surrogates of computationally expensive models. One way of doing so is to use the sparse grid collocation (SGC) methods, which develop polynomials between model state variables and model parameters. Two types of surrogate systems are explored in this study of Bayesian uncertainty quantification for groundwater flow modeling, i.e., the surrogate system for hydraulic head (SG-H) and the surrogate system for likelihood function (SG-L). With respect to SG interpolation error, SG-H is more accurate than SG-L, because the relation between hydraulic heads and model parameters is smoother than that between likelihood and model parameters. Comparing the results of uncertainty quantification, the posterior probability distributions of model parameters and outputs produced by SG-H are more accurate than those by SG-L. Therefore, for complex groundwater model having strong nonlinear and non-monotonic relationship between model parameters and outputs, it is more advantageous to use SG-H than to use SG-L.

papers.title: Active Learning in Fiber Optic Course Using Applied Education Game
papers.abstract: The strategy or method used in the learning process affect the result of learning. The wrong strategy will make students feel bored and lazy to attend class. In general, the learning method that is mostly used in universities around the world is center learning where the lecturer will give speak and the students will listen and take notes. This study was done in two classes i.e. a master’s degree module and a bachelor degree course in the Department of Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering, National University of Malaysia. A total of 31 students were used as respondents (sample) that consists of 61.3% male and 38.7% female, where 41.9% of them are doing bachelor degrees and the other 58.1% doing master’s degrees. This research show that 45% of respondents strongly agree and 55% of respondents agree that education games are more enjoyable than conventional lectures. 68% of respondents strongly agree and 29% of respondents agree that they like to study fiber optic using games. Furthermore, 58% of respondents strongly agree and 39% of respondents agree that they could remember fiber optic principles using the educational game.
